A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WikiCLIP work. All 16 pages, including Appendix A and its image-based results, support reliable comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original WikiCLIP benchmark results in Tables 1–2, ablation experiments, and additional retrieval and representation analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains the original WikiCLIP benchmark experiments, ablations and appendix analyses, including their numerical and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The frozen encoders, Vision-Guided Knowledge Adaptor, hard-negative synthesis, contrastive objective and retrieval procedure are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OVEN training data and evaluate visual entity recognition on OVEN, INFOSEEK and E-VQA. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1, 2, 7 and 9, including AutoVER and CLIP2CLIP on OVEN and Echosight and Google Lens in their respective retrieval comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendix A retain the same splits, preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations and evaluation procedures, including accuracy, harmonic mean and top-k retrieval metrics.

E4.justification: The component ablations, encoder and text-length studies, training-iteration analyses and VGKA architecture comparisons are identical. Appendix A.5 retains the same retrieval examples, error cases, attention visualizations and representation analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 10(b) already presents mean silhouette scores with standard-deviation bars in v3 and is identical in v4. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 and all result figures retain identical values and findings. For example, Table 1 reports WikiCLIP-L's OVEN unseen accuracy of 28.5%, HM of 31.6 and inference latency of 14.49 ms in both versions.

T1.justification: The task formulation, model equations, hard-negative replacement rule, similarity calculation and Appendix A.2 loss definition are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about contrastive recognition, VGKA, hard-negative synthesis, unseen-entity generalization and inference efficiency.

C2.justification: The interpretations of text-length saturation, limited gains from larger LLMs and generalization remain identical. The conclusion's limitations and Appendix A.5's explanations of annotation-related errors are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, training times, FAISS usage and representative-image selection guidance are unchanged. The project-page link target also remains identical.

R1.justification: Reference [31] remains the same NoisyGRPO work, with the same authors, title and citation context; only publication metadata changes. No cited work or substantive research-positioning statement is added or removed.

P1.justification: Reference [31] changes from arXiv:2510.21122 (2025) to Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 38:124239–124267 (2026). The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; main-text and appendix wording and organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Visual changes are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp and local rewrapping/typesetting of reference [31]. Figures 1–10, Tables 1–9, their captions and placement are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 updates one existing reference's publication metadata and the arXiv stamp. The scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and appendices are unchanged, so these limited editorial changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
